pr.title: feat(desktop): Review v2 stage 1 — GitHub slice and Keryx links
pr.body:
Desktop Review v2, stage 1 "GitHub slice and links" (Flow 517). Requirements: `docs/requirements/keryx-desktop-review-v2/` — PRD R1–R3, R5, R6, parts of R4 and R7; decisions D5 and D6. Stage 0 was #1294.

## What changes

- **Pull requests board, GitHub only (R1, R2, D6).** Lanes and order no longer read the local review. Two groupings:
  - "Status" (default): Draft · Waiting for review · Changes requested · Approved. Merged and Closed appear only when the state filter includes them.
  - "My role": Requested from me · Mine · Others.

  Quick filters "Requested from me", "Mine" and "CI failed" sit in the context row, not the toolbar. Lanes the filters rule out are not drawn. Cards are sorted by `updatedAt`, newest first. The attention lane and the "In review" lane are gone, and the card's reason line is built from GitHub data only.
- **Keryx work row on every PR card and list row (R4 part, R7 part).** A fixed 24px row with three slots:
  - Review: `Review · <state>`, from `localReview`, with no round number and no behind count. It opens the current review panel.
  - Flow: `Flow #id · stage`. A Flow counts if its `prUrl` matches or if it is linked to a session bound to the PR.
  - Session: the count of bound sessions. It opens the newest; a menu lists all of them plus "New session".

  An empty slot shows a labelled action instead: "Run review", "Create Flow" or "Open in session". Every card action now has visible text. "Fix review comments" is not included; it is stage 4.
- **Sessions bound to a Subject (R5).** A new `subject` field in the session's `flags.json`, written through `_keryx/session_flags`, records `{kind, repo, number, url}`. Issue sessions get it when `withIssueBinding` binds them.
  - "Open in session" on a PR reopens the newest bound session, or creates one, binds it and prefills the composer with the PR URL without sending.
  - On an older keryx that ignores `subject`, the session still opens, with a notice that the binding was not saved.
  - The session header links back to the PR or Issue and to its Flow.
- **Work from a bound session (R6).**
  - `/review` with no target in a PR-bound session preselects that PR. The started run shows on the card without a refresh.
  - "Create Flow" opens the bound session with a flow prompt. The single new flow package that appears while that request is pending gets linked to the session.
- **Issues (R3, D5).**
  - Default grouping is by GitHub state: Open, plus Closed when the filter includes closed issues.
  - The default source is the project repository: `keryx issues list` with `source: "repository"` reads `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`. "Assigned to me" and the other sources stay selectable, and a stored choice wins.
  - The Flow stage filter is removed; the stage now shows in the card's work row.

No Rust changes.

## Verification

- `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `cd apps/desktop && bun test src`: 1016 pass, 0 fail.
- Root `bunx tsc --noEmit -p .`: clean.
- Root focused suites (`desk-run-store`, `board-badges`, `session/organize`, `shell-session-organize`, `session/issues`, `issues-board`): 67 pass, 0 fail.
- Scenario "PR without Flow and review → Open in session → `/review` → review link on the card" is one integrated App-level test in `ProjectNavigation.dom.test.tsx`. Four product mutations each break it: the preselect, the publish, session reuse and the binding.
- The stage 0 attention set (`carriedAttention`, `seeded`, `seedFor`, `attentionPrs`, `stale`) is unchanged. The one adjacent edited line, the `visible` memo, was mutation-checked.
- The toolbar is unchanged, so the stage 0 measurements still hold.

Not verified:
- No run in the real app with real GitHub data.
- Not checked: the work row in narrow lanes, the session menu placement, the list width (now 1000px).
- Not run: lint, and the Rust CI path.

## Known gaps and choices for the owner

- Deviation (a), team review requests for the tab indicator, stays open: this stage adds no team membership. Deviation (b) is unchanged.
- An Issue has no "another or new session" choice. The issue binding backend keeps one session per issue and account.
- A Flow created outside the pending "Create Flow" window is not linked to the PR until it has a `prUrl`.
- UI choices taken without an owner decision, listed in the flow journal:
  - review slot state words;
  - a disabled "Run review" on a merged or closed PR;
  - the session menu button reads "More";
  - an unsaved new session shows as "not saved yet";
  - "Create Flow" replaces the composer draft;
  - Issue card buttons became work-row links.

Flow package: `.metaproject/flows/517-2026-11-23-desktop-review-v2-stage-1-github-slice-a/`. Still to do: a review-orchestrator round on this PR, and the merge decision.

entries.title: gdctx-flag-allowlist-no-bundle-expansion
entries.summary: A per-flag string allowlist that doesn't expand POSIX-bundled short flags rejects the idiomatic form of a tool's own CLI habits (`-il` vs `-i -l`); expand-then-check, not check-then-reject, for any allowlisted boolean-flag set.

entries.title: Findings reach a review round through the report's keryx:findings block, and a round without one silently records none
entries.summary: `keryx review ingest --report <md>` reads structured findings from a fenced ` ```json keryx:findings ` block inside the report. A report without that block ingests as `findings: in=0`, and every `--verifications` claim naming one of its findings is then discarded as unresolvable — because the finding it names is not in the round.

entries.title: keryx-gdctx-gdgraph-routing-index-cost-not-measured-before-shipping
entries.summary: A mandatory context-injection rule's per-read cost multiplies by every subsequent turn and every subagent dispatch. Measure the re-billed cost across a realistic turn count and subagent fan-out before setting a rule's default scope, not just its one-time size.

entries.title: The keryx on PATH is a stale build; the review pipeline does not exercise the code under review
entries.summary: `~/.local/bin/keryx` is an installed build, and its version lags the working tree. It is NOT the working tree. Every `keryx …` invocation — including `keryx review ingest`, which is how a managed review package is recorded — runs that build, so the review pipeline routinely does not exercise the code being reviewed.

entries.title: A fix round needs its own review: three consecutive rounds each introduced a blocker
entries.summary: On PR #215 (flow 127, project registry) three consecutive review-fix rounds each introduced a new blocker while closing the previous one. The defect was not in any single fix; it was in treating a fix as finished once it addressed the reported symptom.

entries.title: Theme switch repaints already-rendered chrome via old-slot value matching
entries.summary: `/theme` in the OpenTUI shell applied and persisted correctly on 0.2.66, but `applyTheme` (src/tui/shell-chrome.ts) only recolored the chrome's OWN surfaces (renderer background, sidebar border, docks, composer, `/`-menu). Every renderable painted EARLIER with `getTheme()` — transcript frames (user echoes, code-segment boxes, block bodies, side-worker boxes), tone-colored block headers (`theme.error`/`theme.tool`), dock/queue-dock buttons, sidebar panels — kept the old palette's hex in its `borderColor`/`backgroundColor`/`fg` props, so a dark→dark switch (groknight↔tokyonight) looked like "the theme did not apply". Fix: on every `applyTheme`, walk the renderable trees (transcript, docks, sidebarTop, menu, composer, header, footer) and rewrite any prop whose color equals an OLD theme slot hex to the NEW slot hex.

entries.title: A shell allowlist matched against the raw command string is not a security boundary
entries.summary: A remembered glob pattern that is matched against a command string which is then handed to `/bin/sh -c` grants far more than it appears to. The pattern matches text; the shell re-interprets that text. Verified, not theorised: a live allowlist contained `bash *`, `python3 *`, `curl *`, `cd *`, `# *`, `docker *`, `sudo *`, and the exact string `rm -rf /` — each an arbitrary-execution grant that auto-approved with no prompt.

finding.quote:
const step = resolveFlowLink(entry, dirs, session && sessionFlags(session).flow);
      if (step.action === "link") linkRef.current(entry.sessionId, step.dir);
finding.problem: Each pending "Create Flow" entry is resolved on its own against the shared flow directory list: the first directory not in that entry's `knownDirs` is linked to its session. A directory one entry links is never removed from the other entries' candidates, and an entry has no expiry, so it waits for the app's lifetime. `resolveFlowLink` handles "several new packages for one request" but not "one new package, several requests" or "one new package from someone else".
finding.impact: Trigger 1: "Create Flow" on PR A, then on PR B, before A's package exists. `expect` keeps both entries (it only replaces the same sessionId). When A's package appears, both entries see exactly one fresh directory, so both sessions get `flow = A` through `linkFlow` → `_keryx/session_flags`, which writes it to each session's flags.json. Session B's own package appears later, after B's entry was already dropped, so it is never linked. Trigger 2: one pending request while another session in the same checkout, an Issue "prepare-flow", or the CLI creates a flow package. The foreign package is linked. Outcome, persisted: PR B's card shows Flow #A, because `prFlows` adds the flows of bound sessions. Session B's header links to Flow A, and the Flows board lists session B under Flow A. This is silently wrong persisted data (shape 2).
finding.suggested_fix: Claim each directory once across all entries. Resolve the entries in one pass over the fresh directories. When the number of pending entries is not exactly one, or a directory is already claimed, link nothing. Better, attribute positively instead of by arrival: link a package only when its `prUrl` (or a field the flow prompt asks the orchestrator to record, e.g. the session id) matches the request. Give an entry a deadline, for example cleared at the end of the session's first turn after the prompt, so that a package appearing hours later is not linked. Add a usePendingFlowLinks test with two pending sessions and one new package that asserts no link, or only the matching one.
finding.evidence: usePendingFlowLinks.ts: `expect` does `[...old.filter(entry => entry.sessionId !== sessionId), { sessionId, knownDirs }]`, so entries for different sessions coexist. The effect calls `resolveFlowLink(entry, dirs, ...)` per entry with the same `dirs`. prWork.ts `resolveFlowLink` returns `{ action: "link", dir: fresh[0] }` when `fresh.length === 1`, computed only against that entry's `knownDirs`. App.tsx wires `link` to `(id, dir) => void s.linkFlow(id, dir)`. useAcpSession `linkFlow` → `applyPendingFlow` → `client.request(SESSION_FLAGS, { sessionId, cwd, flow })`, and the server's `handleSessionFlags` → `setSessionFlags`, so the link is stored. prWork.ts `prFlows` includes `dirs.has(flow.dir)` from bound sessions. Read the deliberate choice (law 4): the PR body says "The single new flow package that appears while that request is pending gets linked", and the resolveFlowLink doc says several packages link none because "which one is the session's cannot be told". The same reason applies, and is ignored, when one package is visible to several requests or comes from another session. usePendingFlowLinks.dom.test.tsx tests only one pending session.

sites: apps/desktop/src/review/usePendingFlowLinks.ts (effect resolving each pending entry independently; expect without expiry)
apps/desktop/src/review/prWork.ts resolveFlowLink (fresh computed per entry, no cross-entry claim)
apps/desktop/src/App.tsx createPrFlow (the only caller of flowLinks.expect)

finding.problem: The Issue work row is `<div className="pr-work-row issue-work-row">`. Its 2-column override `.issue-work-row` has the same specificity (0,1,0) as `.pr-work-row { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); ... }` in styles/review.css. Same specificity means the rule that comes later wins. main.tsx imports `./App` on line 2, before `./styles/review.css` on line 9. App statically imports IssuesView, which imports IssuesBoard, which imports './IssuesBoard.css'. In Vite dev (style-tag injection in module evaluation order) and in the single-entry build (CSS concatenated in import-graph order), IssuesBoard.css therefore comes before review.css, so the 3-column template should win. The higher-specificity `.issue-table .issue-work-row` sets only min-width and margin-top, so list rows are affected too.
finding.impact: Expected (unmeasured): on every issue card, list row and the issue detail panel, the Flow and session slots each take a third of the row, and the last third stays empty. Each slot is about 2/3 of its intended width, so 'Flow · Needs an answer' and 'Open in session' truncate much earlier than designed. The author's comment ('Two slots ... in the PR work row's fixed-height look') shows two equal halves were intended.
finding.suggested_fix: Raise the specificity so the override wins whatever the load order: `.pr-work-row.issue-work-row { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }`. Alternatively, move the rule into styles/review.css after `.pr-work-row`.
finding.evidence: Static cascade reading: apps/desktop/src/main.tsx lines 2 and 9; App.tsx `import { IssuesView } from "./issues/IssuesView";`; IssuesBoard.tsx `import "./IssuesBoard.css";`; styles/review.css `.pr-work-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); ... }`. keryx ctx rg found no other selector that sets the issue row's columns. Two tracks means the finding is wrong; three tracks with the last one empty confirms it.

finding.problem: Three equal `minmax(0, 1fr)` slots, plus a non-shrinking text 'More' button inside the session slot, in a board lane at its 230px basis (`.review-lanes .lane { flex: 1 0 230px; }`). Hand arithmetic: lane 230 − lane-body padding 16 − flow-card padding 24 and border 2 = 188px card content. (188 − 2 gaps × 4) / 3 = 60px per slot. 'More' ≈ 25px text + 8 padding + 2 border + 2 margin ≈ 37px, leaving the session link 23px border-box, or about 9px of text after its 6px padding and 1px borders. The review and Flow links get about 46px of text each.
finding.impact: Expected (unmeasured), at fs-xs 11px with text-scale 1: 'Open in session', 'Session' and 'N sessions' render as a bare ellipsis. 'Run review' → 'Run re…', 'Review · ready' / 'Review · needs your answer' → 'Review…', 'Flow #517 · In progress' → 'Flow #…'. The state words the row exists to show are never visible; they appear only in the hover title. This is the common case, not a corner. With the default filter (open + draft: 4 lanes), the 1180px default window gives lanes of only about 256px (slot ≈ 69px, session text ≈ 18px). With Merged and Closed drawn, all 6 lanes sit at the 230px basis and the board scrolls. The list-view column (`.review-table th:nth-child(6) { width: 16rem; }`) gives about 75px per slot and has the same session-slot result. A text-scale above 1 makes all of this worse. The PR body lists 'the work row in narrow lanes' as not checked.
finding.suggested_fix: Give the session slot room it can keep. Options: make 'More' an icon-only chevron (16px, keeping its aria-label). Or use uneven tracks, e.g. `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.4fr)`. Or drop the bound-session count to a short form ('2' with an icon) when the slot is narrow. Alternatively, widen `.review-lanes .lane` to a basis where the three default labels fit. Measure 'Open in session', 'Review · needs your answer' and 'Flow #NNN · Needs an answer' at 11px and size the lanes from that.
